title: Oil Prices Fall as Iran Negotiation Hopes Return | OilPrice.com

U.S. sanctions pressure on Iran intensifies, but Pakistani mediation hopes push Brent back to $89.

US Blockade Leaves Iran’s Oil Trade on Borrowed Time

- The announcement of the Trump administration’s ‘Economic D-Day’ sanctions on Iran coincides with an overall slump in Tehran’s crude exports, choked off by the US Navy’s maritime blockade in the Gulf of Oman.

- Iran’s August crude exports have so far been minimal compared to the 2025 average of 1.7 million b/d, averaging only slightly around 0.3 million b/d with only one confirmed loading at the country’s largest terminal in Kharg Island.

- Thanks to the volumes evacuated during the three-week period of free navigation in June-July, Chinese imports of Iranian barrels are slightly above Tehran’s pace of loading, around 800,000 b/d, however due to drawing stocks they are set to decline further next month.

- Should the US maritime blockade of Iran continue, China could run out of Iranian options by October, reflected in soaring Iranian differentials as Iran Light is now traded at a $4 per barrel premium to ICE Brent.

- Iranian floating storage outside of the Gulf has shrunk to just 24 million barrels, down 7 million barrels since the beginning of August, with Chinese buyers mopping up the last remaining volumes.

- US shale pioneer Continental Resources has agreed to acquire privately held Firebird Energy II, boosting its Permian portfolio by 54,000 net acres that currently yield some 32,000 boe/d of oil-weighted output.

- Brazil’s state oil firm Petrobras (NYSE:PBR) has entered direct negotiations with the government of Ghana for exploration contracts covering 4 offshore blocks in the underexplored Keta basin, seeking to expand beyond Brazil.

- US oil major Chevron (NYSE:CVX) has finalized its return to Libya, signing a production-sharing contract covering onshore block S4 in the Sirte basin, containing one 100-million-boe gas discovery and several unconfirmed prospects.

- Guyana’s regulatory body has vowed to investigate a fire that broke out this weekend at ExxonMobil’s (NYSE:XOM) Liza Unity floating production vessel, leading to a suspension in operations.

- The $8 billion sale of Shell’s (LON:SHEL) US chemical assets has drawn interest from several high-profile buyers, with ExxonMobil and LyondellBasell expressing interest along with Kuwait’s state oil firm KPC.

The Trump administration is ratcheting up sanctions pressure on Iran, threatening to sanction all commercial partners of Tehran in case they don’t wind down trade (without specifying the timelines for doing so). At the same time, Pakistan’s mediation efforts have offset the bullish momentum following Scott Bessent’s Monday press conference, with oil market participants still hoping for some form of negotiated settlement, sending ICE Brent prices lower to $89 per barrel.

Washington Takes Its Iran Sanctions War Global. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled the Trump administration’s long-mooted “economic D-Day” measures against Tehran, threatening Iran’s main trading partners, without hinting at China, with exclusion from the dollar system.

Iran Turns Its Hormuz Blacklist into a Contagion Risk. Tehran has threatened fines, detention and cargo confiscation against 45 tankers deemed non-compliant for dark transits through the Strait of Hormuz, warning any vessel conducting ship-to-ship transfers with them could also be listed.

Hormuz Traffic Collapses as Iran Widens Its Shipping Threat. Only 2 commodity vessels crossed the Hormuz strait on Monday, a notable plunge compared to the previous 10-day average of 14, following the Iranian authorities’ threats against dark transits and vessels deemed non-compliant. Saudi Arabia’s Hormuz Bypass Runs into Red Sea Risk. A Houthi attack on the Amzan tanker owned by Saudi Arabia’s national shipping firm Bahri near Riyadh’s only operational loading port of Yanbu exposed the vulnerability of the East-West pipeline, forcing all tankers to move towards the Suez.

IEA Keeps Its Oil Reserve Firepower in Check. The International Energy Agency is not discussing another emergency release after deploying 400 million barrels in March, according to its chief Fatih Birol, claiming to monitor the current situation as 80% of the IEA’s strategic stocks remain intact.

Ukraine’s Drones Keep Russian Diesel Off the Market. According to Russia’s deputy prime minister Alexander Novak, Moscow may extend its diesel export ban through October after a series of Ukrainian drone strikes on southern refineries perpetuated the pressure on domestic fuel balances.

Trump Rebuilds His China Tariff Wall. US President Donald Trump is set to impose an additional 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods over allegations of excess manufacturing capacity, restoring the White House’s second-term duties to 20%, less than a month before the September 24 Trump-Xi Summit.

Britain Eyes an LNG Lifeline as North Sea Gas Fades. The UK government is reportedly considering investment in LNG import capacity amidst declining output, defying calls for a reversal in London’s repressive oil and gas policy that slapped a 78% headline tax under the Energy Profits Levy.

Qatar’s LNG Woes Shift from Gas to Ships. QatarEnergy’s 77 mtpa Ras Laffan liquefaction plant is running short of available gas carriers as the Middle Eastern country’s Hormuz transits have stalled completely, leaving 1.2 million mt LNG afloat in the Gulf and raising the prospect of production cuts.

Iran Finds More Gas, but Not Yet More Supply. Iran has reported the discovery of a giant gas field containing up to 5.7 TCf of recoverable gas, the 2nd significant gas find in the southern province of Fars alongside Pazan, with Tehran aiming for a commissioning date in the second half of 2029.
